Q: How to create a new React project without using additional frameworks? A:

Since create-react-app is deprecated, the React docs now recommend two approaches for client-side React apps without meta-frameworks.
---

Option 1: Bundler-based setup (Vite)

This is the standard approach — a minimal React + TypeScript setup:

npm create vite@latest my-app -- --template react-ts
cd my-app
npm install
npm run dev

Your app runs at: - http://localhost:5173

This gives you a clean starting point. You’ll add routing, styling, API utilities, etc. as needed.

Option 2: Use a preconfigured CLI on top of Vite (optimal)

If you want to avoid repeatedly setting up common production basics (routing, API layer, linting, folder structure, etc.), you can use a preconfigured Vite-based CLI.

npx create-modern-react my-app
cd my-app
npm run dev

This still generates a client-side React + TypeScript app (no meta-framework), but includes commonly used defaults that many teams end up configuring anyway:
• Tailwind CSS + Shadcn/ui components
• Wouter routing with lazy loading
• Axios with interceptors
• ESLint (25+ rules)
• Error boundary
• Path aliases (~/)

Q: How to convert an array of key values to columns in BigQuery / GoogleSQL? A:

Here is my try based on Mikhail's answer here

--DDL for sample view 

create or replace view sample.sampleview
as

with _data
as
(
    select 1 as id,
    array (
        select struct(
            "name" as key,
            "apple" as value
        ) 
        union all
        select struct(
            "color" as key,
            "red" as value
        )
        union all 
        select struct(
            "delicious" as key,
            "yes" as value
        )
    ) as _arr  
    union all 
    select 2 as id,
    array (
            select struct(
                "name" as key,
                "orange" as value
            ) 
            union all
            select struct(
                "color" as key,
                "orange" as value
            )
            union all 
            select struct(
                "delicious" as key,
                "yes" as value
            )
    )
     
    
)
select * from _data

Execute immediate

declare sql string;

set sql = 
            (
                select 
                    concat(
                            "select id,",
                            string_agg(
                                concat("max(if (key = '",key,"',value,NULL)) as ",key)
                            ),
                            ' from sample.sampleview,unnest(_arr) group by id'
                    )
                from (
                    select key from
                    sample.sampleview,unnest(_arr)
                    group by key
                    )
                
            );
execute immediate   sql;

Q: How do I rebase a fork of a fork in Git? Should I? A:

Set up your remotes (if not already done):

cd project-c
git remote add upstream-a https://github.com/original/project-a.git
git remote add upstream-b https://github.com/someone/project-b.git
git fetch --all

2. Create a safety branch:

git checkout -b backup-before-rebase
git checkout main  # or master, whatever your branch is called

3. Rebase onto A:

git rebase upstream-a/main

You'll likely get conflicts where B's changes and A's updates overlap. Resolve them, then:

git add .
git rebase --continue

What This Does

  • Replays your commits (including the ones from B you kept) on top of A's latest code

  • Maintains your custom changes and B's features you need

  • Removes the dependency on the potentially abandoned B project

What It Might Break

  • Merge conflicts: If A changed code that B modified, you'll need to manually resolve

  • API changes: If A updated APIs that B's features depend on, you may need to update B's code

  • Your own code: If your bug fixes depended on B's incomplete features you removed, check they still work
